A 66-year-old woman presents to the emergency room after experiencing a tonic-clonic seizure.
Her medical history is significant for type 2 diabetes mellitus and hypertension for which she takes metformin and losartan.
Her CT scan findings are presented in Figure A.
She is noted to have papilledema on fundoscopy, but physical exam is otherwise normal.
Her temperature is 98.6°F (37.0°C), blood pressure is 115/70 mmHg, pulse is 70/min, and respirations are 12/min.
Recently, she has become increasingly nauseous and has vomited twice in the past 10 days.
She has been having worsening headaches and intermittent nausea over the past 5 months.
